vīlĭcus (less correctly villĭcus), a, um, adj.
villa
,

vīlĭcus, i, m. (sc. homo).
An overseer of a farm or estate, a steward, bailiff; absol., ; ; id. ap. ; ; ; ; ; ; .—With gen.: vilice silvarum et mihi me reddentis agelli,: vilicus Orbi,.—

vīlĭpendo, ĕre, v. a.
vilis-pendo
,

senses: base, vile, mean, worthless, cheap, paltry
la:adj:vilis.html:
vīlis, e, adj.,
of small price or value, purchased at a low rate, cheap (opp. carus).
Lit.: nec quicquam hic vile nunc est nisi mores mali,: annona vilior,: istaec (puella) vero vilis est,: istuc verbum vile est viginti minis,: ex eis praediis talenta argenti bina Statim capiebat ... Ac rebus vilioribus multo talenta bina,: frumentum quoniam vilius erat,: res vilissimae (opp. pretiosissimae),

.—Abl. neutr. (sc. pretio), at a small price, at a low rate, cheaply: Ep. Quanti eam emit? Th. Vili, : vili vendere,.— Comp.: quod viliori praedium distraxerit ... et si non viliori vendidit, etc.,.—Sup.: res stipulatoris vilissimo distracta est,—

Transf.
Of trifling value, cheap, poor, paltry, common, mean, worthless, base, vile (cf. indignus): si honor noster vobis vilior fuisset,: nihil tam vile neque tam vulgare,: Velia non est vilior quam Lupercal,: hi quorum tibi auctoritas est videlicet cara, vita vilissima,: fidem fortunas pericula vilia habere,: nec adeo vilis tibi vita esset nostra, ut, etc.,: et genus et virtus nisi cum re vilior alga est,: inter Perfectos veteresque referri debet an inter Viles et novos?: vilis Europe,vile, abandoned,: tu poscis vilia rerum,: si, dum me careas, est tibi vile mori,.— Neutr. adverb.: et vile virentes Hesperidum risit ramos,i. e. in the ordinary manner,: vile comparati, Schol. .—Prov.: vile est, quod licet,.—
With inf.: stat fucare colos nec Sidone vilior, Ancon. . —
Found in great quantities, abundant, common (poet. and rare): poma,: phaselus,.—Hence, adv.: vīlĭter.
Lit., cheaply: venire poteris intestinis vilius,: vilissime constat,: vilissime constiterit,.—
Transf., meanly, poorly, vilely: se ipsum colere,; : vilissime natus,.

vīlĭtas, ātis, f.
vilis

Lit.: tanta repente vilitas annonae ex caritate rei frumentariae consecuta est, etc.,: vilitas in vendendis (fructibus),: cum alter annus in vilitate, alter in summā caritate fuerit,, § 216: ad denarios senos vilitas rediit,: offerre aliquid vilitati,to offer for sale at a low price,.—

la:verb:vilico.gloss: to act as an overseer or bailiff (over)
senses: to act as an overseer or bailiff (over)
la:verb:vilico.html:
vīlĭco (villĭco;
perf. and sup. perh. not found), āre, 1, v. n. and a.; and vīlĭ-cor, ātus sum, āri, 1., v. dep.
vilicus
.
Neutr.
To act as bailiff, overseer; to superintend (prop. of a country estate).
Form vilico: dispensare rem publicam, et in eā quodammodo vilicare,.—
Form vincor: non vilicari, sed dominari mea est sententia, Pomp. ap. (Com. Rel. v. 45 Rib.): longe ab urbe vilicari, quo erus rarenter venit, p. 186, 1: hic vilicor ante urbem: nunc rus eo, Turp. ap. (Com. Rel. v. 82 Rib.).—
Transf., to live or reside in the country.
Absol.: in Arpinos jam ... explodam hominem, ut vilicetur, Afran. ap. .—
With adv. of place: ego nondum etiam hic vilicabar, Turp. ap. .—
With abl.: vilicatus praediis,.—
Act., to manage an estate, etc., as a bailiff, etc.: possessionem maximam illam vilicabat,.
